findings.checklist_item: Specify the corpus->ItemRecord adapter as explicit work (not 'wiring only'): how each corpus item's outcome maps to decision block/advisory/dropped and its gold `label`, plus how the ParityReport is serialized/recorded — following the existing fidelity_spot_eval.py precedent (_record/_records + record_results).
evidence: parity.py:40-56 ItemRecord requires valid/decision/label per item; parity.py:104-107 scores decision agreement + gold flips on that
search_files: parity_report has no corpus-adapter caller in src/rebar

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:165-194,225-241 shows the equivalent adapter (ItemRecord with gold label, epochs/majority) that must be written, plus record_results serialization at :279 — evidence this is real logic, not 'wiring only'
Ticket 0d76 research comment (verified at HEAD): 'there is NO ItemRecord adapter ... Building that mapping is NET-NEW work and it is load-bearing, because criterion (b) ... is scored on it'
findings.finding: The plan's claim 'No new gate logic is written; this story supplies the corpus run and records the report' (and Scope's 'wiring only if the driver needs a provider parameter') understates the mechanism: parity_report() consumes per-item ItemRecord(valid, decision, label), but nothing in the standing eval corpus emits ItemRecords. There is no production caller that maps the corpus to ItemRecords (search_files finds only container_fidelity_report/prerequisite_fidelity_report/parallel_run_and_diff/fidelity_spot_eval), run_eval yields per-epoch pass/fail (not per-item decision+gold label), and there is no serializer for the recorded report. Building the corpus->ItemRecord adapter (which decision each corpus item maps to, and its gold label) is net-new and LOAD-BEARING, because criterion (b) 'zero decision-level flips' is scored entirely on that mapping.
findings.location: Approach ('No new gate logic is written'); Scope ('src/rebar/llm/parity.py — no logic change expected; wiring only')
scenarios: Implementer reads 'wiring only', writes no adapter, and cannot produce a scoreable ParityReport
Ad-hoc decision-mapping is chosen inconsistently, so criterion (b)'s flip count is meaningless
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the fidelity_spot_eval.py pattern: run each corpus item through both arms, map the gate verdict to a decision, carry the gold label, average over epochs, feed paired ItemRecord lists to parity_report, and serialize the report to a committed artifact / ticket comment.

findings.checklist_item: State how the run reaches >=20 gold-labelled items (pool gold across specs, or explicitly pass and justify a lower min_gold), and forbid a cases cap that would truncate the gold sources below the floor.
evidence: parity.py:88 MIN_GOLD_ITEMS = 20; parity.py:92 default min_gold=MIN_GOLD_ITEMS; parity.py:133-134 appends 'gold set too small to certify ...' failure

Ticket 0d76 research comment (verified): 'No single eval spec's gold_set reaches 20 — the largest is plan-review-container at 12. So the driver MUST pool gold items across specs, or explicitly lower min_gold and justify it'
findings.finding: The mechanism cannot produce a PASS as specified because parity_report enforces a gold-coverage floor the plan never provisions: parity.py sets MIN_GOLD_ITEMS=20 (the default min_gold) and appends a gating failure when fewer than 20 items carry a gold label in {block,advisory,dropped} (parity.py:133-134). No single eval spec's gold set reaches 20. The plan does not say the driver must pool gold items across specs (or lower min_gold with justification), so a naive per-spec run fails the gold-coverage guard regardless of Bedrock's actual parity.
findings.location: Approach ('Run the existing parity_report machinery with the standing eval corpus'); Scope
scenarios: A per-spec run yields n_gold < 20 and the report FAILS on coverage, not on any Bedrock regression, masking the real signal
REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES=12 truncation decapitates the largest gold sources and trips the floor

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify HOW the N≥3 repeats are collected and averaged into each ItemRecord, since parallel_run_and_diff runs each item once — either name the repeat-aggregation as a driver wiring step (a to_record/runner that averages N draws) or state which harness performs the averaging before parity_report is called.
evidence: Plan: 'v2 = Bedrock-hosted Claude … same model family and decoding params, N≥3 repeats — the protocol parity.py already documents. No new gate logic is written; this story supplies the corpus run'
parity.py:42 ItemRecord docstring: 'One runner's outcome on one corpus item (averaged over the N repeats).' — the averaging is asserted but not implemented

parity.py:296-301 parallel_run_and_diff: `for item in corpus: for runner, sink in ((run_v1, v1), (run_v2, v2)): sink.append(to_record(item, runner(item), False))` — one call per (item, runner); no repeat loop, no aggregation
search of parity.py for 'repeat' returns no matches — the N≥3 protocol has no implementing code
findings.finding: The plan asserts the 'N≥3 repeats' protocol is 'already documented' by parity.py and that running 'the existing parity_report machinery' suffices, but the N≥3 repeat-averaging exists only in parity.py prose (module docstring line 6; ItemRecord comment line 42 'averaged over the N repeats') and is NOT implemented by the record-producing driver: parallel_run_and_diff (lines 286-302) runs each corpus item exactly once per runner with no repeat loop or averaging. An executor following the plan literally would produce single-shot ItemRecords, silently failing the N≥3 requirement the deliverable AC mandates.
findings.location: Approach ('N≥3 repeats — the protocol parity.py already documents'); Scope ('parity.py — no logic change expected; wiring only if the driver needs a provider parameter'); AC line 1 ('N≥3 repeats')
scenarios: Executor wires v1=Anthropic/v2=Bedrock into parallel_run_and_diff as-is, runs the corpus once, and attaches a ParityReport that is single-shot, not N≥3-averaged — the AC's 'N≥3 repeats' is unmet while appearing satisfied.
A per-item verdict that is non-deterministic across repeats (the very reason N≥3 exists) is captured from a single draw, so a flaky decision-level flip either hides or fires spuriously.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope/Approach, add the repeat-aggregation seam explicitly: e.g. 'the live job runs each corpus item N≥3 times per provider and passes averaged ItemRecords (valid = majority/mean, decision = modal outcome) into parity_report; parallel_run_and_diff itself runs once per item, so the N≥3 loop lives in the job wiring, not in parity.py.'

Ticket 0d76 research (verified at HEAD): the ladder is class-based [trivial/standard/frontier]; a working two-provider recipe exists via REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE [llm.model_classes] pinning frontier on one provider and standard/trivial on the other, exercised end-to-end (41 opus + 1 bedrock split)
Ticket 0d76 research: 'Both arms would then differ in TWO variables (provider AND per-pass model class), which makes any criterion failure unattributable and any pass unrepresentative of production'
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'paired runs differing only in provider' and 'same model family and decoding params', but does not specify how that isolation is achieved given the gate's per-pass model ladder/class mapping. Simply setting REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<id> flips provider AND the per-pass model class at once (Pass-1 frontier vs verifier standard), so any criterion (a)/(b) failure is unattributable and any pass is unrepresentative of production. The protocol must pin per-pass model CLASSES identically on both arms so provider is genuinely the only variable — the plan omits this.
findings.location: Approach ('same model family and decoding params'); Testing ('paired runs differing only in provider')
scenarios: A criterion fails and no one can tell whether Bedrock or a mis-paired per-pass model caused it
Both arms pass on a sonnet-only comparison that never exercises the opus Pass-1 path production uses
findings.suggested_fix: Drive both arms via REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE [llm.model_classes] pinning each per-pass class to the paired Anthropic/Bedrock model, and use the REBAR_USAGE_LOG per-call model rig to assert the v2 arm hit no Anthropic-provider calls.
